question.value: What is the complete millimeter structure of the Fomalhaut outer debris disk (geometry, eccentricity, width, azimuthal structure, apocenter glow), and what is the stellar flux at 1.3 mm?

claims.hypothesis: Does the complete disk at 1.3 mm show apocenter glow?
claims.experiment: Uniform-sensitivity mosaic and eccentric ring model; compare NW and SE flux
claims.result: ~65 uJy (>5 sigma) NW-SE difference; flux ratio 1.10+-0.02
claims.finding: First conclusive detection of apocenter glow

evidence.quote: we note a significant flux difference between the apocenter (NW) and pericenter (SE) sides of the disk of $\sim65$ $\mu$Jy ($>5\sigma$)

claims.hypothesis: What are the belt geometry, width and eccentricity?
claims.experiment: MCMC fit of eccentric particle model to visibilities
claims.finding: Narrow, radially confined eccentric belt consistent with prior results

evidence.quote: The outer belt is radially confined with an inner edge of $136.3\pm0.9$ AU and width of $13.5\pm1.8$ AU.

claims.hypothesis: Are previously reported azimuthal features present?
claims.result: No significant peaks except the background galaxy
claims.finding: Previous HST, SCUBA, ALMA features not confirmed

evidence.quote: Our observations do not confirm any of the azimuthal features found in previous imaging studies of the disk with HST, SCUBA, and ALMA.

claims.hypothesis: Is the stellar 1.3 mm flux consistent with photospheric models?
claims.experiment: Fit star as point source and compare with PHOENIX
claims.finding: Star is fainter than photospheric prediction

evidence.quote: The central star is clearly detected with a flux density of $0.75\pm0.02$ mJy, significantly lower than predicted by current photospheric models.

claims.experiment: Combine alpha_mm with apocenter/pericenter ratios vs Pan et al. simulations
claims.finding: beta constrained, consistent with Draine relation

evidence.quote: consistent within $1\sigma$ with the $\beta\simeq (q-3)\beta_s$ quoted by (cite: dra06)

why_this_data.value: Mosaic designed to cover the whole ring with equal sensitivity to examine azimuthal structure

evidence.quote: The ALMA 1.3 mm mosaic map of the outer Fomalhaut debris disk was designed to cover the complete ring with equal sensitivity, allowing us to examine azimuthal structure along the belt.

why_this_method.value: Mm observations trace large grains unperturbed by radiation forces; orbit-based model accounts for eccentric particle orbits

evidence.quote: the large grains that emit predominantly at these wavelengths are not significantly perturbed by radiation forces and better trace the location of the larger planetesimals

limitations_admitted.value: Resolution (~10 AU) prevents constraints on edge sharpness; Δa and e_p degenerate; large uncertainty on ω from inclination degeneracy

evidence.quote: we are unable to place any strong constraints on the sharpness of the disk edges.

limitations_admitted.value: 2D model ignores vertical structure, which could loosen width constraints

evidence.quote: Adding a vertical component to the model would likely loosen the constraints we are able to place on the width of the belt

Different observing executions with different weather combined without stated relative scaling
